strengths: Comprehensive empirical characterization of the knowledge-prediction gap across 5 models and 11 diverse MCQ benchmarks with consistent findings
Clean geometric interpretation using knowledge/prediction subspaces with clear visual evidence (Figure 3) demonstrating misalignment
Technically sound constrained optimization method (KAPPA) with closed-form solution and rigorous mathematical derivation
Consistent improvements across diverse task categories (1.5-16.9% gains on reasoning/bias benchmarks) with lightweight inference-time approach requiring no retraining
Careful experimental design addressing confounds (32 prompt formats), appropriate baselines (CAA, DoLA), and ablation studies demonstrating causal relationships
Well-structured presentation with logical flow from motivation through analysis to solution
weaknesses: Scope limited to linearly accessible knowledge; while pragmatically justified, this restricts insight into actual model failures and knowledge representations may encode information non-linearly
Severely limited generalization: cross-dataset transfer is poor (Section 5.1), requiring dataset-specific probe training and limiting practical applicability to new tasks
Free-form generation results contradict generalizability claims—degraded performance on GSM8k (91.6%→90.7%) when applying KAPPA beyond MCQ format with insufficient explanation

Methodological choices lack justification: 85% prediction accuracy threshold for layer selection is arbitrary, 'top-n consecutive layers' criterion is ad-hoc, and fixed hyperparameters (α=30) aren't tuned per-dataset
Limited mechanistic understanding of *why* the gap exists; paper mainly offers vague hypotheses about knowledge override rather than investigating underlying causes
Modest absolute improvements on many benchmarks (e.g., 47.8%→49.6% on GSM8k) with knowledge benchmarks showing negligible gains; large gap between method performance and knowledge probe upper bounds
Insufficient reproducibility details: no code availability statement, probe selection involves subjective choices, lacks error bars/confidence intervals, and needs ablation on key thresholds
Limited comparison with recent representation engineering and steering methods beyond CAA/DoLA; missing analysis of how effectiveness scales with model size

strengths: Comprehensive empirical study across 5 models and 11 diverse benchmarks demonstrating the knowledge-prediction gap is systematic and structural
Novel geometric interpretation via knowledge/prediction subspaces in residual stream, providing interpretable structure to the phenomenon
Principled, inference-time intervention (KAPPA) with closed-form solution that adapts per-instance rather than applying fixed corrections
Rigorous experimental methodology with multiple prompt formats, proper train/val/test splits, and comparison against relevant baselines (CAA, DoLA)
Well-motivated two-probe approach (knowledge vs. prediction) with complementary metrics (AGR, KLD) capturing different aspects of alignment
Insightful cross-dataset transfer analysis revealing when subspace transfer succeeds based on shared underlying skills
Practical and deployment-friendly approach requiring no model retraining, applicable to existing models at inference time
weaknesses: Limited novelty of core observation—the knowledge-prediction gap was identified in concurrent recent work (Marks & Tegmark 2024; Orgad et al. 2025); main contribution is characterization and application rather than discovery
Significant generalization limitation: task-specific probes required for each domain, undermining practical utility. Cross-dataset transfer shows limited success outside same-category tasks
Modest absolute improvements in many settings (GSM8K Qwen: +1.4%, MMLU: <1-2 points) despite strong motivation; improvements concentrated on truthfulness/bias rather than reasoning/knowledge
Limited scope of free-form generation results (Table 4): only +2.5% TruthfulQA, −0.9% GSM8K, weakening claims of generalization beyond MCQs
Fundamental reliance on linear knowledge assumption without empirical validation that non-linear knowledge isn't more important
Causality incompletely established: improvements could stem from other transformation aspects (regularization, exploration); ablation studies on orthogonal directions absent
Layer selection criterion somewhat arbitrary (highest knowledge probe accuracy where prediction >85%); sensitivity analysis limited, unclear how much results depend on this choice
Hyperparameter choices (α=30, β=0 for single-layer) claimed as 'without tuning' but clearly matter (Figure 4), suggesting some task-dependence
Missing ablations: random subspace controls, effect of subspace dimensionality, how performance scales with probe quality
No error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance testing across multiple runs

strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation across 11 benchmarks, 5 model families (4B-32B), with consistent improvements and rigorous statistical testing including sensitivity analyses on distractor sampling and data size

Novel geometric interpretation revealing knowledge and prediction signals route along nearly orthogonal directions (≈90°) at intervention layers, with strong correlation (ρ=0.976 for Llama 3.1 8B) between principal angles and behavioral gap

Rigorous experimental methodology: careful prompt engineering to avoid positional biases, complementary metrics (AGR and KLD), multiple random seeds, and thorough mechanistic analysis showing KAPPA operates via abstract intermediate representations rather than direct logit manipulation
Consistent improvements in agreement rates up to 22.2 percentage points over baselines, with substantial gains on truthfulness/bias benchmarks (8.9-16.9 points for LLaMA 3.1 8B)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (particularly Figure 1), sound mathematical derivations, and comprehensive appendix enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: Method addresses only linearly accessible knowledge with no empirical assessment of non-linear knowledge; fundamental limitation not adequately explored

Causality between geometric misalignment and behavioral gap shown through correlation only (Figure 10), not proven causation; the mechanism linking subspace alignment to performance improvements is assumed rather than theoretically justified

Severe practical limitation: Figure 5 shows limited cross-dataset transfer requiring dataset-specific probe training for each task, fundamentally limiting real-world applicability without principled transfer solutions
Improvements modest on knowledge-intensive benchmarks (Table 11) where gap is smallest; method most effective where problem already pronounced, raising questions about broader utility
Incomplete understanding of gap origins: speculations about hasty answering and trace leverage are untested; why knowledge and prediction subspaces diverge during training remains unexplained
Hyperparameter selection (α=30 single-layer, α=10 multi-layer) appears arbitrary without principled guidance; extended alignment formulation (Eq. 4) lacks theoretical justification
Free-form generalization inconsistent (TruthfulQA +2.5%, GSM8k -1%; Table 4); overstated claims of generalization beyond MCQs given mixed results and LLM-as-judge evaluation limitations
Computational cost of intervening at intermediate layers during generation not analyzed; critical for assessing deployment feasibility
No characterization of failure modes or guidance on when KAPPA should not be used; missing analysis of how gap relates to model training procedures and what knowledge types are most affected
